paragraphs: **Rabbi Yossi ben Meshulam. (A tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.)**

In [Terumot 4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Terumot.4.7), Rabbi Eliezer says that terumah is neutralized in a mixture of one hundred and one parts. Rabbi Yehoshua says: “In one hundred and a little more”; this additional amount has no fixed measure. Rabbi Yossi ben Meshulam says that its measure is a kav.[^1] This is also explicitly stated in the Jerusalem Talmud there. In [*Darkhei ha-Mishnah*, page 201, note 9](https://hebrewbooks.org/pdfpager.aspx?req=31828&st=&pgnum=210&hilite=), the author says that *Seder HaDorot* was mistaken on this point. With all due respect, however, he himself was mistaken, because he did not consult the Jerusalem Talmud there.

He is also mentioned in [Bekhorot 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bekhorot.3.3), where he says: “One who slaughters a firstborn animal makes room with a cleaver on either side and plucks the hair”—and likewise plucks the hair in order to see the site of a blemish. At the beginning of [chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bekhorot.6.1), he says that “dried out” means that it crumbles.[^2] (From this we learned the criterion for the species used with the lulav, as in [Sukkah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.29b), and for a lung, in [Chullin 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.46b.8-10).[^3]) Maimonides wrote that he is mentioned only once in the Mishnah; perhaps he had a different textual reading.

He was a colleague of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya. Thus, in [Chullin 57b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.57b), Rabbi Yossi ben HaMeshulam says: “There was an incident in Inbul—”; Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar replies: “Do you bring proof from there?” and so forth. The same account appears in [Tosefta Oholot 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Oholot.2.4).

He and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya were called “the holy congregation,” as in [Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.2.4). The reason for this designation is explained in [Kohelet Rabbah 9:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.9.9): they divided the day into three parts—one third for Torah study, one third for prayer, and one third for work. Some say that they devoted themselves to Torah study in winter and to work in summer.

In [Menachot 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.62a), he disagreed with Chanina ben Chakhinai and Rabbi [Judah the Patriarch]. In [Gittin 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.62a), he testified in the name of his brother Rabbi Yochanan, who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar Chasma. In [Tosefta Demai, at the beginning of chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai.3) and in [chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai.6), the text has “in the name of his brother Rabbi Natan”; it should read “Rabbi Yonatan.”[^4] In Tosefta Kelim, chapter 6, and [Makhshirin, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Makhshirin.2), we find: “Abba Yossi ben Dukhai and Rabbi Yossi ben HaMeshulam say…”.[^5]

He is also mentioned in [Chullin 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.15b); Bekhorot 25 and [39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.39b); and Sifrei, Ekev, section 1.[^5] In [Yalkut Shimoni, Matot, on “on the day he hears”](https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/ילקוט_שמעוני_מטות), Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: “I asked Rabbi Yossi ben Meshulam and Yehoshua ben Gamla.” This is undoubtedly a textual error.[^6]

notes.text: *Terumah* is the priestly portion of produce. The first formulation means one part terumah mixed with one hundred parts of ordinary produce, one hundred and one parts in total. A *kav* is a measure of volume. Hyman abbreviates the Mishnah’s fuller formulation.
The Mishnah discusses a firstborn animal’s ear that has dried out sufficiently to constitute a blemish: it must crumble. Hyman’s parenthesis applies that criterion to other discussions.
Hyman’s “Sukkah 46b” should be **Chullin 46b:8–10**, linked in the translation.
“It should read Rabbi Yonatan” is **Hyman’s proposed correction**. The earlier “Rabbi Yochanan” and the reported Tosefta reading “Rabbi Natan” remain distinct.

Hyman gives no division of Tosefta Kelim or folio side for Bekhorot 25. The modern location corresponding to “Sifrei, Ekev, section 1” remains uncertain. Makhshirin is read as continuing the preceding Tosefta reference.

Hyman abbreviates the speaker as אר״א״בי, rendered Eliezer ben Yaakov. The linked Yalkut reading is **Yonatan ben Meshulam**, whereas Hyman quotes **Yossi ben Meshulam**. “This is undoubtedly a textual error” is Hyman’s judgment; he supplies no explicit replacement reading.
